title: Mobile, portable and solar stations
blurb: Explain what mobile antenna parts do, how to power and quiet a mobile radio, and how solar panels charge a battery safely.

G4E01.why: A capacitance hat **electrically lengthens** a physically short antenna, helping it resonate on a lower frequency.
G4E01.trap: It doesn't reduce radiation resistance or lower the radiation angle.

G4E02.why: A rounded ball spreads the field at the tip, so **RF voltage discharge** from a sharp end is reduced.
G4E02.trap: It limits RF discharge. It isn't a crash guard and doesn't narrow bandwidth.

G4E03.why: 100 W takes heavy current, so connect **to the battery with heavy-gauge fused wire**. A balanced transmission line carries RF, not DC power.

G4E04.why: The socket is wired for small loads, so its **wiring may be inadequate** for the radio's current.
G4E04.trap: Polarity and engine heating aren't the issue.

G4E05.why: Efficiency of the **electrically short antenna** is the biggest HF mobile limit: radiating power matters more than wire gauge.
G4E05.trap: Wire gauge is fixable. There is no such FCC mobile power limit.

G4E06.why: A short antenna has very high Q, so its **bandwidth is very limited** and it needs retuning when you change frequency.
G4E06.trap: Short antennas have high Q, not low.

G4E07.why: Charging system, fuel delivery and control computers are each noise sources: **all of these**.

G4E08.why: One cell gives only about half a volt, so cells are in **series for voltage and parallel for current**: series-parallel.

G4E09.why: A lit silicon cell's open-circuit voltage is about **0.5 V**, which is why panels string cells in series.

G4E10.why: With no light the panel is a dead load, so the diode **blocks battery discharge through the panel**.
G4E10.trap: Regulating voltage and limiting current are charge-controller jobs, not the diode's.

G4E11.why: LiFePO4 must be charged within limits, so the panel needs a **charge controller** to regulate charging.
G4E11.trap: A series resistor can't regulate charging, and grounding or placement don't help.
